_comment: The GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, as requirements a tool can check rather
than a logo on a marketing page. The tool already computed to the standard;
it never told a preparer whether their inventory would actually satisfy it.
Each requirement carries the field or condition that satisfies it, so the
conformance check is data-driven and a reader can see why it passed.
ghgprotocol.org could not be reached from the build environment, so this is
drawn from professional-firm and practitioner summaries of the standard and
graded medium. Verify against the Corporate Standard before relying on a
standard: GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (Revised Edition)

sources.title: A Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (Revised Edition)
Key requirements of the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard

principles.name: Relevance
principles.note: The inventory reflects the emissions of the company and serves the decision-making needs of its users.

principles.name: Completeness
principles.note: All emission sources within the chosen boundary are accounted for, and any exclusion is disclosed and justified.

principles.name: Consistency
principles.note: Methodologies allow meaningful comparison over time; any change in method, boundary or data is documented.

principles.name: Transparency
principles.note: Assumptions, references and methodologies are disclosed so a reader can follow the number to its source.

principles.name: Accuracy
principles.note: Quantification is neither systematically over nor under actual emissions, so far as can be judged.

organizational.name: Equity share
organizational.note: Emissions accounted according to the share of equity in the operation, reflecting economic interest.

organizational.name: Financial control
organizational.note: 100% of emissions from operations under financial control; nothing from operations held but not financially controlled.

organizational.name: Operational control
organizational.note: 100% of emissions from operations where the company has authority to introduce and implement operating policies.

boundaries.note: The choice must be disclosed, and applied consistently. Changing it is a structural change that triggers base-year recalculation.

requirements.name: Organisational boundary stated
requirements.why: A reader cannot interpret a total without knowing which entities are inside it. The standard requires the consolidation approach to be disclosed, not merely chosen.

requirements.name: Operational boundary stated
requirements.why: Scope 1 and Scope 2 are the minimum. A company reporting Scope 3 must also list the activity types covered by it.

requirements.name: Scope 2 reported location-based and market-based
requirements.why: The Scope 2 Guidance requires both. A market-based figure alone hides the grid the company actually draws on; a location-based figure alone hides the contracts it has signed.

requirements.name: Base year stated
requirements.why: Targets and trends are meaningless without the year they run from. The standard requires a base year — a specific year or an average of several — to be established and disclosed.

requirements.name: Base year recalculation policy stated, with a significance threshold
requirements.why: Structural changes, methodology changes and discovered errors all trigger recalculation. Without a stated threshold, the decision to recalculate is made after the number is known — which is the wrong order.

requirements.name: GWP assessment set stated
requirements.why: The same activity yields different tonnes under AR4, AR5 and AR6. A total without its assessment set cannot be compared with anything.

requirements.name: Exclusions disclosed and justified
requirements.why: Completeness does not require reporting everything; it requires saying what was left out and why. An unstated exclusion is the difference between an incomplete inventory and a misleading one.

requirements.name: Methodologies and emission factors disclosed
requirements.why: Transparency. Every calculated figure must trace to the factor applied, its source and its vintage.

requirements.name: Gross emissions presented separately from any offsets or trades
requirements.why: The standard requires gross emissions for the chosen inventory boundary to stand separate from and independent of any GHG trades. Netting them makes the inventory unusable.

requirements.name: Scope 3 screened across all fifteen categories
requirements.why: Scope 3 is optional under the Corporate Standard, but a partial Scope 3 presented without saying which categories were screened reads as a complete one.

requirements.name: Data quality or uncertainty assessed
requirements.why: A total carries no information about how much of it is measured and how much estimated. The standard asks for an uncertainty assessment; this tool scores data quality 1–5 and rolls it up emissions-weighted.

requirements.name: Verification status stated
requirements.why: Whether the figures were checked by anyone independent, and to what level, changes what a reader may rely on them for.

scope2.note: The GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance requires both a location-based figure, using average grid emission factors for the area consumption occurs in, and a market-based figure, reflecting contractual instruments the company has purchased. Both are reported; neither replaces the other.

scope3.note: Scope 3 is optional under the Corporate Standard itself, and the reason to report it is rarely the Corporate Standard — IFRS S2 paragraph 29(a), ESRS E1-6 and CSRD's value chain provisions all require it. A partial Scope 3 must say which categories are in and which are out.
